text:
This looks like late 2021. Fed funds is at 0.08%, CPI is 5.38% YoY, core CPI is 4.04%, unemployment is 4.8%, and the 10-year yield is 1.57%. US large-cap equity is up 41% over 12 months and up 7% in the last month, which fits October 2021 (S&P up about 7% that month). The 12-month figure also fits, since October 2020 was a dip.

Unemployment was 4.6% in October 2021 and 4.8% in September 2021, but the release lag may explain the difference. Payrolls averaged about 550k over 3 months. Core CPI at 4.04% fits September 2021 (4.0%), and headline CPI at 5.4% also fits September. Industrial production YoY at 4.6% fits September. So the data were published through September, while the market data run through October. The 10-year yield of 1.57% fits the end of October 2021 (about 1.55%). The 2-year at 0.50% also fits October.

The snapshot is therefore October 2021.
